name: Memory B cell
markers: IgM, IgG, IgA or IgE on the surface (its B-cell receptor)
CD80, PD-L2 (CD273) and CD73 (mouse marker for class-switched memory cells)
summary: A B cell that survives an earlier immune response, long-lived and quiet, ready to act fast if the antigen returns. Its antibody is mutated and often class-switched, so it binds better than a naive B cell's, and it divides sooner. On re-exposure most become plasma cells that make antibody within days.
functions: Is made in two ways: in germinal centres, carrying mutated and usually class-switched antibody, and early, outside them, mostly keeping IgM with few mutations (shown mainly in mice).
Persists without the antigen: it can survive for years, probably decades in humans, as a resting cell. In humans, memory B cells after smallpox vaccination have been found up to 50 years later.

On meeting its antigen again, it divides and differentiates faster than a naive B cell. Most become plasma cells within days, which gives the quicker, larger secondary antibody response. It usually needs help from memory CD4 T cells.

Debated: how many memory B cells re-enter germinal centres on a second exposure. In mice, boosting gives limited re-entry from a restricted set of clones, so most of the response arises from the memory cells directly.

Is not one cell type in mice: IgM-bearing and IgG-bearing memory cells behave differently on recall, with IgM cells more ready to re-enter germinal centres and IgG cells to become plasma cells quickly.
Debated: where human CD27-positive IgM memory B cells come from, with one view that they are circulating marginal zone B cells and another that they come from germinal centres.
Recirculates through blood, spleen and lymph nodes, and some stay in tissue: after influenza in mice, resident memory B cells settle in the lung and need local antigen to form.
abundance: About a third of B cells in adult human blood are memory cells (CD27-positive), rising with age; babies have few. Laboratory mice, kept clean, have few memory B cells until they are immunised.
